name: Telecom, IT and information services

bnote.611001: India's listed telecom operators. Reliance Jio sits inside Reliance Industries and is not listed separately.
bnote.611002: India's listed cable companies belong to the Reliance group, which is already counted, so large US cable companies are used.
bnote.611099: The three largest US mobile carriers.
bnote.619003: Tanla and Route Mobile send business SMS and alerts in India. Twilio and Sinch are the global leaders.
bnote.621100: Nazara is listed under Section J. Take-Two and Roblox are large listed game developers.
bnote.621901: India's listed mid-size IT services companies. LTIMindtree, Tech Mahindra and Cyient are left out because their parents are already counted.
bnote.622001: India's four largest IT services companies, plus Accenture.
bnote.631001: E2E Networks runs a GPU cloud in India. Microsoft and Oracle are large cloud providers.
bnote.631006: Anant Raj is building data centres in India. Equinix is the largest colocation provider.
bnote.639002: Info Edge (Naukri) and IndiaMART run Indian internet portals. Meta runs Facebook and Instagram.

flags.idea: Net profit is boosted by a one-time gain from government relief on dues, so net margin and P/E are not operating results.
flags.googl: Net profit is above EBITDA because of large gains on investments.
flags.naukri: Net profit includes gains on its investments (such as Zomato), so it is above EBITDA.
flags.crwd: Profit is near zero after stock-based pay, so P/E and EV/EBITDA are not meaningful.
flags.panw: Profit is small after stock-based pay, so P/E is not meaningful.
flags.e2e: Revenue is small and growing fast, so the valuation multiples are very high.
flags.mtnl: MTNL is loss-making and carries heavy debt.

notes: India is strong in IT services and telecom. Cloud, search and social media use US companies. Software products were covered under Section J.
